description:
## Question

Prototype the compile errors for a set of rejected constructs (a map, a string, recursion, an array through an if, an unsupported Enum function, a type mismatch) and react to them: location, why it's rejected, the suggested alternative, and how it links to docs/language.md.

comments.text:
Prototype: branch prototype/compile-errors, prototypes/compile_errors_prototype.exs (run: elixir prototypes/compile_errors_prototype.exs [A|B|C|D]). Six rejections (map, string, recursion, array through if, Enum.map, return-type mismatch) in four styles; every suggested rewrite was compiled and run against defk at main. Today's messages for map and string have no line and echo `:a` / `"hello"`; Enum.map gives no why or alternative.

Resolution (style D):
- Layout: Elixir's diagnostic frame (error: line, caret block, └─ file:line:col: Mod.fun/arity), then `why:` and `hint:` on their own lines (rewrite indented below the hint), then `(defk <code>: docs/language.md#<code>)`.
- Name the Elixir construct as written ("Enum.map/2 is not in the kernel subset", "maps are not ..."), caret under the whole construct.
- Permanent vs planned in words: "not in the kernel subset" vs "not supported yet"; no ticket IDs in user-facing text (the reference entry says what is planned).
- Rewrites use the developer's own code where the compiler has it cheaply (return type, array in a branch), a template otherwise. A suggestion must compile: every rewrite in the reference is tested (see "How are kernels checked against Elixir mode?").
- Error codes are readable slugs (unsupported-call, array-in-branch, recursion, ...), doubling as docs/language.md anchors, never renamed.
- Report every rejection in the module, capped at 10; suppress errors caused by an earlier one.
Build handed off as "Adopt the kernel compile error format".

title: What does a good kernel compile error look like?
